Figure 5-1 The most demanding condition analyzed; Transport condition with jack-ups + ice Final Technical Report 24/57 6 CEC SUPPORTING STRUCTURE DESIGN The MTV lifecycle, based on the operations required along the device life, helps to understand the conditions at which the CEC supporting structure works and, thus, the requirements for its design. The CEC supporting structure working conditions under MTV lifecycle can be outlined in the stages below: 1. Installation: this stage corresponds to the CEC loading on the vessel with the help of an external crane (Figure 6-1). MTV is located in sheltered waters (negligible EC), and the CEC is loaded and fastened onto the sliding deck, which has adjustable cradles for this purpose. This sliding deck uses a rail-wheel system, allowing for positioning of the CEC below the tube of the supporting structure, where it is bolted to it ready for transportation (Figure 6-1). 2. Transportation: the MTV transports the CEC until the deployment site. The CEC is fastened to the sliding deck and the flange of the CEC supporting structure (Figure 6-1). This operation is performed under benign EC. 3. On site. In this stage, the tube slides downwards with the help of a rack-pinon system, positioning the CEC at the required position to start operating. 4. Testing: 2 conditions may occur during this condition. o Survival conditions: the CEC is placed onto the sliding deck while the vessel is moored, withstanding extreme conditions o Operating conditions where the CEC may operate under defined EC under two configurations (Figure 6-2): ▪ Jack up tower configuration: nacelle center 5 m below MSL, being turbine blades always below MSL. This configuration is meant to be used in the rivers considering sufficient an air gap of 2 m ▪ Moored configuration: nacelle center 4 m below MSL, avoiding possible turbulences with the hull 5. Maintenance: as in the transport condition but with negligible environmental loads, the CEC is fastened to the sliding deck and the flange of the CEC supporting structure. Final Technical Report 25/57 Figure 6-1 Left: Handling stage Right: Transport stage Below: Detail of the transport stage Figure 6-2 CEC positioning for both configurations under operating conditions left: jack up tower right: moored The final design is accomplished by applying ABS regulation, to the largest extent possible, verifying the design against ULS, ALS, and FLS limit states according to the LRFD design methodology. If this is not possible due to the lack of data, additional offshore standards (DNV, API) are applied. The analysis methodology to validate the design is mainly the FEM. The structure resistance against strength and buckling failure (ULS, ALS) is provided by an overall system stiffness behavior, allowing for design under a conservative E.C. envelope. On the other hand, fatigue failure (crack initiation) is caused by notch features within the structure where the loads shall be analyzed accurately.
